items.denn: denn also gives a reason, but the verb then stays in second place: …, denn ich bin krank. Here bin is last: weil.
items.deshalb: deshalb is an adverb that gives a result, not the reason, and it does not send the verb to the end.

items.weil: weil sends the verb to the end. Here the verb stays in second place: denn.
items.obwohl: obwohl means „although“. It would also send the verb to the end, and the meaning is wrong.

items.Weil: weil starts a Nebensatz and sends the verb to the end. Here the verb comes right after the first word.
items.Denn: denn joins two clauses after a comma. It cannot start a new sentence like this.

items.Trotzdem: trotzdem takes the verb right after it. Here regnet is at the end, so it needs a conjunction: obwohl.
items.Aber: aber stands outside the clause and does not send the verb to the end.

items.Obwohl: obwohl sends the verb to the end. Here gehen follows directly.
items.Weil: weil gives a reason and sends the verb to the end. Here the sentence is a contrast.

items.Wenn: wenn is for repeated events or for the present and future. One event in the past is als.
items.Wann: wann is a question word (when?), not a conjunction for statements.

items.Als: als is for one event in the past. This is a general present: wenn.
items.Ob: ob means „whether“ and opens an indirect question.

items.wenn: wenn means „if“ or „whenever“. The sentence asks whether he comes: ob.
items.dass: dass reports a statement. Here there is a yes/no question.

items.ob: ob means „whether“. After glauben a statement is reported with dass.
items.das: das with one s is an article or pronoun. The conjunction is dass.

items.dass: dass reports a fact. It does not give a purpose.
items.um: um … zu needs the same subject and an Infinitiv. Here du verstehst has its own subject.

items.damit: damit needs its own subject in the second clause. With the same subject use um … zu.
items.dass: dass reports a statement, not a purpose.

items.aber: aber gives a contrast. After a negation, the correct item takes sondern.
items.oder: oder offers an alternative. It does not correct the negation.

items.So: so belongs to other patterns (so … wie). The pair here is je … desto.
items.Wenn: wenn means „if“. The pair opens with je.

items.der Bus hat Verspätung: weil sends the verb to the end. Here hat stays in second place.
items.hat der Bus Verspätung: Verb first is a question order. weil needs the verb at the end.

items.der Bus Verspätung hat: denn keeps normal word order, so the verb stays in second place.
items.hat der Bus Verspätung: Verb first is a question order. After denn the order is normal.

items.ich komme später: deshalb takes the first position, so the verb comes next and the subject after it: komme ich.
items.ich später komme: Verb-last order belongs to weil, dass and similar words. deshalb does not send the verb to the end.

items.wir reiten aus: A Nebensatz at the start fills the first position, so the verb comes next: reiten wir.
items.wir aus reiten: The verb must stay in second place in the main clause, and the prefix aus goes to the end: reiten wir aus.

items.kommt er morgen: After ob the verb goes to the end: ob er morgen kommt.
items.er kommt morgen: ob opens a Nebensatz, so the verb goes to the end.

items.aber: nicht nur … sondern auch is a fixed pair. aber does not fit.
items.und: und simply adds. The pair needs sondern.

items.weder: weder pairs with noch and means „neither“. With oder the pair is entweder … oder.

items.als: als compares or marks one past event. The second part of je … is desto.
items.so: so … wie compares things. je pairs with desto.

items.obwohl: obwohl would send the verb to the end. Here hat es follows directly: dennoch.
items.sondern: sondern follows a negation. It cannot mean „nevertheless“.

items.damit: damit gives a purpose. so … dass gives a result.
items.weil: weil gives a reason. so leise … dass shows the result.

items.nachdem: nachdem means „after“ and is about the order of events, not a contrast.
items.damit: damit gives a purpose, not a contrast.

items.hatte: ankommen forms its Perfekt with sein, so it is war, not hatte.
items.ist: ist is the present. The sentence is in the past: war.

items.sodass: sodass gives a result, not a condition.
items.damit: damit gives a purpose, not a condition.

items.sodass: sodass gives a result. zumal adds a second reason.
items.obgleich: obgleich means „although“. The sentence adds a further reason.
